decisions.word: מֵאֶלֶף (first of the pair; a second אֶלֶף follows)
decisions.evidence: Under the alef of the first word is a three-dot segol cluster. It has the same shape as the segols under the following אֶלֶף. There is no vertical stroke, so it is not a T-shaped qamats. The second אֶלֶף is fully inside the crop, with segol under the alef and the lamed.

No sheva is printed under the first yod. In the same crop the sheva under וְלֹא is clearly visible as two stacked dots, and nothing like it appears under ויי. The only marks under ויי are horizontal strokes (patah under the vav, plus a mark under the second yod). This matches בַּייָ on s95.
A dot is visible inside the pe's mouth, with hiriq below. The dagesh is present.

The mark under the first mem has a horizontal stroke next to the two dots, which makes it a hataf patah. A plain sheva would have no stroke. Confidence is moderate, so a human may want to spot-check it.

The large type is clear. There is a patah under the he and a dagesh in the mem. Under the mem is a segol with a separate vertical tick to its left, which is a printed meteg. The two stacked dots at the final kaf sit inside the kaf's open area, under its top bar and left of the descender, so they are the kaf's sheva. Nothing is printed in the empty margin of roughly 45px to the left of the kaf, so there is no sof-pasuq colon.

The bet has a T-shaped qamats with a visible vertical. Under the resh is only a horizontal bar with no vertical, which is a patah. The two shapes are easy to tell apart side by side. A colon follows the final kaf.
The alef of אתה has a T-shaped qamats, so the form is pausal, and the tav has qamats with dagesh. The alef of אלא has a segol and the lamed has qamats with dagesh. A colon follows.
